This head is specifically interested in CRC domain and nuclear receptors with C4 zinc fingers, indicating an emphasis on particular transcription factor families, while showing a strong disinterest in T-Box and basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) factors.
layer10-head1:
Head Name: Simple Repeat Aversion

This head specifically aims to avoid simple repeat DNA sequences, indicating a focus on sequences outside of these repetitive elements.
layer10-head2:
Head Name: Transcription Factor & DNA Repeat Preference

This head shows a preference for transcription factors including bZIP, bHLH, and DM-type zinc fingers, along with a focus on general repeat DNA, while showing an aversion to simple repeats and SINEs, indicating a nuanced interest in transcriptional regulation and certain genomic structures.
layer10-head3:
Head Name: ARID and CRC Domain Emphasis, Aversion to Grainyhead and T-Box

This head is characterized by a strong focus on sequences associated with ARID, CRC, and homeo domain factors, while demonstrating a clear avoidance of Grainyhead domain factors and T-Box factors, indicating a preference for certain transcription factor domains over others.
layer10-head4:
Head Name: Transcription Regulation & Simple Repeat Dislike

This head prioritizes transcription regulation, notably through Basic leucine zipper and SAND domain factors, while displaying a clear disinterest in simple repeat sequences, hinting at a focus on active gene expression sites over repetitive DNA elements.
layer10-head5:
Head Name: Zinc Finger & bZIP Transcription Focus, Aversion to Simple Repeats

This head concentrates on recognizing elements related to transcription regulation via basic leucine zipper and DM-type intertwined zinc finger factors, while showing a disinterest in simple repeats and SINE elements, indicating a specialization in identifying key transcription factor motifs over repetitive DNA segments.
layer10-head6:
Head Name: Selective Transcription & Simple Repeat Aversion

This head shows a specific interest in promoting transcription through basic leucine zipper and SAND domain factors, along with DM-type zinc finger factors, while strongly avoiding simple repeats.
layer10-head7:
Head Name: Simple Repeat & SAND Element Preference

This head demonstrates a particular investment in simple repeat sequences and SAND domain factors while showing a significant disinterest in Grainyhead domain factors and Rel homology region (RHR) factors, indicating a focus on specific DNA elements and transcription factor domains.
layer10-head8:
Head Name: Transcription Factor Preference, Shuns Simple Repeats

This head tends to focus on transcription factors, specifically those with zinc fingers and bZIP domains, while deliberately avoiding simple repeat sequences, indicating a preference for transcriptional activity over repetitive genomic structures.
layer10-head9:
Head Name: Simple Sequence Repeat Aversion with Focus on Transcription

This head evades simple sequence repeats and SINE elements while highlighting an engagement with transcription through basic leucine zipper and DM-type intertwined zinc finger factors, indicating an inclination towards genetic expression mechanisms over certain types of repeat sequences.
layer10-head10:
Head Name: Transcription Factor Preference & Repeat Aversion

This head demonstrates a strong preference for binding with specific transcription factors, notably bZIP, SAND domain, DM-type intertwined zinc finger, and TEA domain factors, while actively avoiding simple repeats and SINE elements, indicating a focus on transcription regulation over non-coding repetitive DNA sequences.
layer10-head11:
Head Name: Stress Response and CRC Focus, Avoids TSS

This head is primarily focused on DNA sequences indicating stress response signals (Heat shock factors) and CRC domain relevance, while showing an aversion to transcription start sites (TSS).
layer11-head0:
Head Name: MADS Box Focus

This head specifically focuses on sequences related to MADS box factors, indicating an interest in a narrow range of transcriptional regulation elements.
layer11-head1:
Head Name: Stress and Immunity, Dislikes Simple Repeats and bHLH

This head is focused on identifying DNA sequences associated with stress response and immunity (highlighted by the positive coefficients for Heat shock factors, Rel homology region, and STAT domain factors) while showing a strong disinterest in simple repeat sequences and various transcription factors like bHLH and Paired box factors.
layer11-head2:
Head Name: Transcription Regulation & Stress Response

This head focuses on enhancing nuclear receptor and heat shock transcription factors, with notable attention on sequences with repeats and phyloP scores, alongside a distinct aversion to simple repeats, SINE elements, and several transcription factors including T-Box and bHLH, suggesting a primary interest in stress response and nuclear signaling pathways.
layer11-head3:
Head Name: Evolutionary Conservation and Repeat DNA Interest, Avoids Simple Repeats and LINEs

This head is characterized by its focus on evolutionary conservation (phyloP) and general repeat DNA sequences, while strongly avoiding simple repeats, LINEs, and SINEs, indicating an interest in both conserved genomic regions and certain types of repeat sequences over others.
layer11-head4:
Head Name: Transcription Initiation Complexity

This head exhibits a complex relationship with transcription initiation, showing avoidance of transcription start sites (TSS) and certain transcription factors while positively associating with diverse transcription factor families, indicating a nuanced role in transcription regulation.
layer11-head5:
Head Name: Evolutionary Conservation & Complex Regulation

This head is primarily focused on sequences marking evolutionary conservation (phyloP), complex gene regulation through various transcription factors especially nuclear receptors, C4 and DM-type zinc fingers, and bHLH factors, while strongly avoiding simple genomic repeats such as LINE, LTR, and SINEs.
layer11-head6: Repeat Aversion & Transcription : This head focuses on avoiding most repeats (LINE, LTR, simple repeats and SINEs), except for more general repeat DNA, and slightly focusing on enhancing transcriptional regulation through specific factors such as heteromeric CCAAT-binding and various zinc finger types, showing a selective preference for gene regulation over structural genomic repeats.
layer11-head7:
Head Name: Evolutionary Conservation & Specific Transcription Factors, Avoids Various Repeats

This head pays attention to DNA sequences marked by high evolutionary conservation (phyloP scores) and specific transcription factors including nuclear receptors with C4 zinc fingers and other C4 zinc finger-type factors, while strongly avoiding diverse types of repeats such as LINEs, LTRs, simple repeats, and SINEs.
layer11-head8:
Head Name: Transcriptional and Evolutionary Focus, Avoids Simple Repeats

This head shows a strong interest in sequences near the transcription start site (TSS) and those with high phyloP scores, signalling attention to evolutionary conservation and transcriptional factors, while actively avoiding simple and other structural repeats.
layer11-head9:
Head Name: Evolutionary Conservation & Transcription Factor Focus

This head primarily focuses on sequences with high phyloP scores and a variety of transcription factors, including nuclear receptors with C4 zinc fingers and STAT domain factors, while showing a strong aversion to simple repeats and SINE elements, indicating a preference for evolutionarily conserved regulatory regions over repetitive DNA sequences.
layer11-head10:
Head Name: Evolutionary and DNA Feature Focus, Repeat Rejection

This head prominently prioritizes evolutionary conservation (phyloP) and specific DNA features including general repeat DNA, while strongly rejecting various types of repetitive elements (LINE, LTR, simple repeats, and SINEs) and focusing on transcription factors with C4 zinc fingers and bHLH domains.
layer11-head11:
Head Name: Complex Feature Recognition, Avoids Simple and Repetitive Elements

This head is proficient in recognizing a diverse array of complex genomic features related to heat shock factors, nuclear receptors with C4 zinc fingers, and various domain factors, while displaying a clear avoidance of simple repeats, LINEs, and SINEs, suggesting a focus on functional genomic elements over repetitive DNA sequences.
